Extract elements that appear multiple times

Source: R/multiple.R
multiple.Rd

Similarly to unique, multiple returns a vector with only the values that appear several times, i.e. that are actually duplicated.

Usage

multiple(x, single = FALSE, na.rm = FALSE)

Arguments

x

A vector.

single

Logical, whether to actually return only values that appear a single time, i.e. the opposite of multiple (defaults to FALSE).

na.rm

Logical, whether to remove NAs. Defaults to FALSE, i.e. NA is considered a value of its own.

Value

An object of the same type of x, but with only the values that appear several times.

Author

Mathieu Basille mathieu@basille.org

Examples

(toto <- rep(c(1:4, NA), times = 1:5))
#>  [1]  1  2  2  3  3  3  4  4  4  4 NA NA NA NA NA
unique(toto)
#> [1]  1  2  3  4 NA
multiple(toto)
#> [1]  2  3  4 NA
unique(nsubset(toto, 2)) # `nsubset(x, 2)` keeps only values that occur at least twice
#> [1] 2 3 4

## Argument 'single'
multiple(toto, single = TRUE)
#> [1] 1
unique(nsubset(toto, 2, comp = "<"))
#> [1] 1

## Argument 'na.rm'
unique(toto, na.rm = TRUE)
#> [1]  1  2  3  4 NA
